cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, is back down from Mount Sinai, where he's been talking with the LORD. Now he gathers the whole congregation of Israel. EVERYBODY. He's got things the LORD has commanded them to do.

cards.question: Moses starts with the week. Six days of work, and then the seventh day is a holy day, a Sabbath of complete ___ to the LORD.

cards.text: And this is serious, friend. Whoever does any work on that day must be put to death.

cards.question: On the Sabbath, the people can still light a fire in their homes.

cards.text: Then Moses moves on to something new. The LORD has commanded an offering.

cards.question: Moses tells the people who should bring this offering to the LORD. Who is it?

answers.text: Every man twenty years or older

cards.text: Then comes the list: gold, silver and bronze, blue, purple and scarlet yarn, fine linen, goat hair, ram skins dyed red, fine leather, acacia wood, olive oil, spices, onyx stones and gemstones. Back on the Millers' counter, ONE new cookie cutter was a big day. This list would've knocked me right off the counter.

cards.question: The LORD wants more than materials. Who does Moses call to come and make everything the LORD has commanded?

cards.text: And it's EVERYTHING: the tabernacle and its tent, the ark and its mercy seat, the table, the lampstand, both altars, the basin, the courtyard curtains, all the way down to the tent pegs and ropes. Plus the holy garments for Aaron the priest and his sons.
Then the whole congregation of Israel walks away from Moses. Friend, I've seen a room clear out after a big meeting, and I KNOW how that usually goes.

cards.question: After they leave Moses, the people whose hearts are stirred come back with an offering to the LORD.

cards.text: And here they come, men and women both. The first thing hitting the pile is gold.

cards.question: What kind of gold do the men and women bring to the LORD?

cards.text: Whoever has yarn, linen, goat hair, ram skins or leather brings it. Whoever has silver, bronze or acacia wood brings that too. NOBODY is sitting this one out.

cards.question: The skilled women spin yarn, linen and goat hair with their own hands and bring what they've spun.
The ___ bring the onyx stones and gemstones for the ephod and breastpiece, plus spices and olive oil.
All the men and women whose hearts prompted them bring a ___ offering to the LORD.

cards.text: Then Moses says the LORD has called Bezalel son of Uri, of the tribe of Judah, by NAME. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer just hoping somebody would remember mine.

cards.question: The LORD has filled Bezalel with the ___ of God, along with skill, ability and knowledge.

cards.text: Bezalel can design in gold, silver and bronze, cut gemstones and carve wood. Me? I press dough. That's the WHOLE résumé.
The LORD has also gifted Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan. Two guys for this whole build? Friend, that's a LOT of tent pegs.

cards.question: The LORD gives both Bezalel and Oholiab the ability to ___ others.
The LORD fills Bezalel and Oholiab with skill to work as embroiderers and weavers too.

cards.text: So Moses says it plainly: Bezalel, Oholiab and every skilled person are to carry out everything the LORD has commanded. Then he summons them all.

cards.question: The workers Moses summons are people whose hearts stirred them to come and do the work.

cards.text: Moses hands the craftsmen all the contributions the Israelites brought, and the work begins. But the people? They're not finished.

cards.question: How often do the people keep bringing freewill offerings for the sanctuary?
With offerings still coming in every morning, what do all the skilled craftsmen working on the sanctuary do?

answers.text: They leave their work to talk to Moses
They ask for more gold and silver
They call for more workers to help

cards.question: The craftsmen tell Moses the people are bringing more than enough for the work the LORD commanded.

cards.text: Moses gives an order, and they send a proclamation all through the camp. Everybody stop what you're doing, this one's OFFICIAL.

cards.question: What does the proclamation throughout the camp tell the men and women?

answers.text: No one should make any more offerings
Everyone should bring twice as much
Only the leaders should bring more

cards.text: So the people are held back from bringing more. Friend, have you EVER heard of a fundraiser begging people to STOP giving? EVER?
What they already have is more than enough to do all the work. Hold on to your aprons, friend, because this story's not done.

findings.problem: The opening card has four sentences: 'Moses... with the LORD.' 'Now he gathers...' 'EVERYBODY.' 'He's got things...'. The limit is three.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: The card says Moses is back down from Mount Sinai after talking with the LORD. That fact comes from Exodus 34:28-29, which is outside the passage. The card cites only Exodus 35:1, so the outside fact has no reference.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The card says 'The LORD has commanded an offering.' The offering is named in Exodus 35:5, not 35:4. The card cites only Exodus 35:4, so its citation is too narrow.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: This summary card for the materials list (Exodus 35:5-9) names every item one by one instead of saying in a few words what the stretch covers.

rule.text: He says in a few words what it covers and doesn't go item by item.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences. The limit is two.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This summary card for the list of things to make (Exodus 35:11-19) walks through the items one by one: tabernacle, tent, ark, mercy seat, table, lampstand, altars, basin, curtains, tent pegs, ropes and garments. It should say in a few words what the stretch covers.

rule.text: He says in a few words what it covers and doesn't go item by item.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences. The limit is two.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: 'NOBODY is sitting this one out' is stated as fact, not as a joke. Exodus 35:23-24 says everyone who had these materials brought them. It does not say every person gave.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The story card has four sentences: 'Bezalel can design...' 'Me?' 'I press dough.' 'That's the WHOLE résumé.' The limit is two.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences. The limit is two.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: 'Two guys for this whole build?' implies only Bezalel and Oholiab do the work. The text shows that is wrong: every skilled craftsman is called (Exodus 35:10), the skilled women spin (35:25-26), and every skilled person carries out the work (36:1-2).

rule.text: He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: '...and the work begins.' 'But the people?' 'They're not finished.' The limit is two.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The setup line 'Everybody stop what you're doing, this one's OFFICIAL' reads like the content of the proclamation. It signals 'stop', which gives away the answer to card 14 and rules out 'Everyone should bring twice as much' and 'Only the leaders should bring more'.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: 'So the people are held back...' 'Friend, have you EVER heard...?' 'EVER?' The limit is two.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
